label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea.
unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea as an eleven-year-old orphan mistakenly adopted by the elderly siblings Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. Despite initial reluctance from Marilla, Anne's joyful spirit and imagination win them over, and she settles into farm life while making a lifelong best friend in Diana Barry. After years of academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe and various humorous misadventures, she earns a scholarship to Queen's Academy and passes her teacher's license examinations with distinction. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne postpones her college ambitions to stay at Green Gables and teach at the Avonlea school so Marilla will not lose her eyesight or home. After two years of teaching and helping found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, she leaves for Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Diana, Priscilla Grant, and Gilbert. During her college years, Anne lives at Patty's Place, declines a marriage proposal from the wealthy Roy Gardner upon realizing she does not truly love him, and earns her B.A. degree. When Gilbert falls critically ill with typhoid fever, Anne confronts her true feelings and ultimately accepts his proposal of marriage after his recovery.

unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea as an eleven-year-old orphan mistakenly adopted by the elderly siblings Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. Despite initial reluctance from Marilla, Anne's joyful spirit and imagination win them over, and she settles into farm life while making a lifelong best friend in Diana Barry. After years of academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe and various humorous misadventures, she earns a scholarship to Queen's Academy and passes her teacher's license examinations with distinction. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne postpones her college ambitions to stay at Green Gables and teach at the Avonlea school so Marilla will not lose her eyesight or home. After two years of teaching and helping found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, she leaves for Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Diana, Priscilla Grant, and Gilbert. During her college years, Anne lives at Patty's Place, declines a marriage proposal from the wealthy Roy Gardner upon realizing she does not truly love him, and earns her B.A. degree. When Gilbert falls critically ill with typhoid fever, Anne confronts her true feelings and ultimately accepts his proposal of marriage after his recovery.

unit: Anthony Pye attends the Avonlea school when Anne Shirley takes over as the schoolteacher in Anne of Avonlea. Despite the advice of others like Mrs. Rachel Lynde to whip him, Anne chooses to win him over with patience, kindness, and fairness. Eventually, Anthony's hostility melts, and he becomes one of Anne's most loyal and devoted pupils, even defending her to others.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina enters the narrative during Anne Shirley's second year at Redmond College.
unit: Aunt Jamesina enters the narrative during Anne Shirley's second year at Redmond College, when Anne, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon decide to rent Patty's Place in Kingsport. Stella arranges for her Aunt Jamesina to join them as their chaperone and housekeeper. Upon arriving, Aunt Jamesina instantly wins the affection of all four girls with her bright disposition, humor, and domestic skill. She brings along her two cats, Joseph and Sarah, and creates a warm, welcoming home for the students throughout their college years. Over the course of their stay, she acts as a wise and sympathetic advisor during the girls' various romantic dilemmas and life decisions. When the girls graduate and Patty's Place is given up, Aunt Jamesina prepares to return to her brother's home, remaining deeply fond of Anne and the rest of the group.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grows up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews grows up in Avonlea as the brother of Jane, Prissie, and Nettie Andrews. During his school days, he is a quiet student who rarely participates in the imaginative games of Anne Shirley and her friends. As he grows into young adulthood, he takes up farming in Avonlea and becomes a solid, respectable worker. In Anne of the Island, Billy decides he wants to marry Anne Shirley, but he is far too timid to propose to her himself. Instead, he sends his sister Jane to deliver his proposal of marriage on his behalf. Anne promptly and politely declines the indirect offer, which Billy takes in stride without much lasting heartbreak, eventually moving on to marry Nettie Blewett.

unit: Billy Andrews grows up in Avonlea as the brother of Jane, Prissie, and Nettie Andrews. During his school days, he is a quiet student who rarely participates in the imaginative games of Anne Shirley and her friends. As he grows into young adulthood, he takes up farming in Avonlea and becomes a solid, respectable worker. In Anne of the Island, Billy decides he wants to marry Anne Shirley, but he is far too timid to propose to her himself. Instead, he sends his sister Jane to deliver his proposal of marriage on his behalf. Anne promptly and politely declines the indirect offer, which Billy takes in stride without much lasting heartbreak, eventually moving on to marry Nettie Blewett.

label: History
value: Davy and his twin sister Dora arrive at Green Gables.
unit: Davy and his twin sister Dora arrive at Green Gables in Anne of Avonlea after their mother passes away, and Marilla Cuthbert agrees to foster them temporarily. While Dora is quiet and perfectly behaved, Davy immediately turns Green Gables upside down with his misbehavior, such as locking Dora in the tool house or putting a toad in the cellar milk pans. He quickly forms a deep bond with Anne Shirley, who manages his upbringing with patience, affection, and imaginative stories rather than strict discipline. When the distant relative who was supposed to take them dies, Marilla decides to adopt Davy and Dora permanently. Throughout Anne's time at Redmond College in Anne of the Island, Davy sends her humorous letters detailing his life, school, and antics in Avonlea. As he grows older, he begins to mature slightly under Marilla and Anne's guidance, though his lively spirit remains intact.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley.
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley in childhood and the two swear an oath of eternal friendship, becoming bosom friends. Her mother temporarily forbids their friendship after Diana accidentally becomes intoxicated on raspberry cordial at Green Gables, but the ban is lifted after Anne saves Diana's younger sister, Minnie May, from croup. Diana attends the Avonlea School alongside Anne and later joins the Avonlea Youth's Improvement Society. Unlike Anne, Diana does not pursue higher education at Queen's Academy or Redmond College, remaining in Avonlea. She becomes engaged to Fred Wright and marries him while Anne is attending Redmond College. By the end of Anne's time at Redmond, Diana has settled into married life and given birth to her first child, a son named Anne Cordelia Wright.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables after their mother, Mary Keith, passes away. While Davy constantly gets into mischief, Dora quickly proves to be a model child who never causes any disruption. When their wealthy relative Uncle Richard dies without leaving them money as expected, Marilla decides to adopt both children permanently. Dora grows up quietly at Green Gables under Marilla's care while Anne Shirley leaves for Redmond College. She continues her schooling and routine life in Avonlea, remaining a steady, reliable presence at home.

label: History
value: Gilbert first meets Anne Shirley at Avonlea School.
unit: Gilbert first meets Anne Shirley at Avonlea School, where he famously pulls her red hair and calls her 'Carrots,' earning a slate smashed over his head and years of cold resentment from her. Despite Anne's grudge, Gilbert consistently attempts to apologize and protect her, competing with her academically throughout their school years and at Queen's Academy. Upon graduation from Queen's, he selflessly resigns his position as Avonlea's schoolteacher so Anne can stay at Green Gables after Matthew Cuthbert's death, which finally breaks the ice between them and initiates a close friendship. He later attends Redmond College alongside Anne, where he excels academically and in student life while continuing to harbor romantic feelings for her. During their junior year, Gilbert proposes to Anne, but she rejects him, claiming she only cares for him as a friend, which causes a painful distance between them. After graduating from Redmond, Gilbert contracts a life-threatening case of typhoid fever, which causes Anne to realize her true feelings for him. Upon his recovery, Gilbert learns of her changed heart and proposes to her a second time at Hester Gray's garden, where she happily accepts him.

label: History
value: Mr. James A. Harrison moves to Avonlea
unit: Mr. James A. Harrison moves to Avonlea and buys the farm neighboring Green Gables. His first encounter with Anne Shirley is contentious when her jersey cow, Dolly, breaks into his wheat field, leading to a fiery exchange of insults. However, the two quickly overcome their bad start and become close friends, often sharing tea and conversations. He confides in Anne about his parrot, Ginger, whose profane language causes Mr. Harrison much embarrassment. When Ginger unexpectedly dies, Mr. Harrison buries him quietly, though he secretly misses the bird. Later, his estranged wife, Emily Harrison, unexpectedly arrives in Avonlea, revealing that Mr. Harrison was married all along. Through Anne's peacemaking and Emily's domestic influence, the couple resolves their past differences and reunites, turning their household into a neat and happy home.

value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's close childhood friends and a member of the Story Club. She attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne, Ruby Gillis, and Diana Barry, successfully obtaining her teacher's license. After graduating from Queen's, Jane taught at Newbridge School and later at other island schools, earning a reputation as a conscientious teacher. In 'Anne of the Island', while Anne attends Redmond College, Jane accepts a marriage proposal from a wealthy Winnipeg millionaire named Edward Inglis. Her sensible approach to marriage contrasts sharply with Anne's romantic ideals, but Jane expresses quiet happiness in her choice before moving west to start her married life.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis met Stephen Irving
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis met Stephen Irving in her youth and fell deeply in love, but their pride led to a misunderstanding and a broken engagement. Stephen left the region, eventually married another woman, and had a son named Paul, while Miss Lavendar remained unwed at Echo Lodge in Grafton. Years later, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon Echo Lodge by accident and immediately bonded with Miss Lavendar over her whimsical nature. Anne later introduced Miss Lavendar to Paul Irving, who took a great liking to her. After Stephen Irving returned to Prince Edward Island, Anne facilitated a reunion between Stephen and Miss Lavendar. The two rekindled their romance, reconciled their past mistakes, and were happily married at Echo Lodge before departing for Boston.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables in Avonlea with his unmarried sister, Marilla. Deciding they need help with farm chores as Matthew grows older, they arrange to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. When Matthew goes to the Bright River train station to fetch the child, he finds eleven-year-old Anne Shirley instead, as a mistake had been made. Despite his paralyzing shyness, Matthew is immediately charmed by Anne's imaginative talk during the ride home and quietly insists to Marilla that they keep her. Over the next several years, Matthew acts as Anne's devoted confidant, secretly spoiling her with treats like a dress with puffed sleeves. When Anne earns a scholarship to Queen's Academy and later passes her exams with distinction, Matthew takes immense pride in her achievements. Shortly after Anne returns home for the summer, Matthew suffers a fatal heart attack upon reading that the Abbey Bank, where his life savings were deposited, has failed. His love and belief in Anne leave a lasting impact on her life, prompting her to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, after spending his earlier childhood in the United States. When Anne Shirley becomes the Avonlea schoolteacher, she quickly recognizes Paul as a exceptionally gifted pupil and a kindred spirit. label: History
value: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school.
unit: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school. On Anne's first day, he severely humbles and embarrasses her by misspelling her name on the blackboard and forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe as punishment for being late. His harsh and public punishments lead Anne to refuse to attend school for several months. Throughout his tenure, he openly woos one of his oldest students, Prissy Andrews, paying far more attention to her than to his instructional duties. At the end of his school term, he leaves Avonlea, much to the relief of most of his students.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner meets Anne Shirley
unit: Roy Gardner meets Anne Shirley during their time at Redmond College, famously sharing an umbrella with her in the rain. Captivated by her, he begins an earnest, romantic courtship, frequently sending her dark pink roses and spending time with her at Patty's Place. Anne initially believes he is her ideal romantic hero because of his good looks, wealth, and gallant behavior. Over two years, Roy courts Anne with the full approval of his family and friends, leading up to a grand proposal of marriage in his final year at Redmond. However, when he proposes, Anne realizes that she does not truly love him because he lacks real emotional depth and a shared humor, prompting her to reject his proposal. Devastated and humiliated by her refusal, Roy departs, bringing their relationship to a permanent end.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's primary classmates and joined the Story Club in her girlhood. She later attended Queen's Academy with Anne and their peers, successfully obtaining a teacher's certificate before taking up a teaching position outside Avonlea. Throughout her adolescence and early adulthood, Ruby was famous for having more 'beaux' than any other girl in her circle, constantly talking of romance and marriage. However, her life was cut short when she contracted galloping consumption (tuberculosis). Returning home to Avonlea, she spent her final summer sitting in her family's garden, trying to ignore the gravity of her illness. Shortly before her passing, she shared a poignant heart-to-heart conversation with Anne, confessing her fear of heaven because it lacked the familiar romance and frivolity she cherished. She passed away peacefully during the night at the end of the summer.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy comes to Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy comes to Avonlea to replace Mr. Phillips as the teacher at the Avonlea school. Her modern teaching methods initially raise some eyebrows among the conservative members of the community, but her success with the children quickly wins everyone over. She organizes a special Queen's Class to prepare her brightest pupils, including Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. Under her tutelage, all of her candidates pass with flying colors. Although she eventually leaves Avonlea for a new teaching position, she remains a beloved mentor and role model in Anne's life.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard first met Anne Shirley at Queen's Academy in Charlottetown.
unit: Stella Maynard first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while studying at Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where they became close friends. After teaching for a time, Stella decided to pursue a Bachelor of Arts degree at Redmond College in Kingsport, joining Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon. Seeking a comfortable alternative to boarding houses, Stella proposed setting up a shared home, bringing her aunt, Aunt Atossa (Aunt Jamesina), to act as housekeeper and chaperone. Together, the four young women rented a charming cottage named Patty's Place, where they lived happily throughout their remaining college years. Stella completed her studies at Redmond and graduated alongside Anne and her friends.
